content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides UNDERDETERMINED by citing two different senses/answers to Matthew 1:20, which is the situation the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed whether two senses leave the matter open for UNDERDETERMINED, or whether both senses must stand and the verse is not open; the rule requires the latter.","why":"The judge treats Matthew 1:20's covenant-presence and physical-source readings as leaving the issue UNDERDETERMINED, but K-S2 forbids treating a verse with two senses as open and requires both senses to stand."}
